title: Platform systems & services: playbook, how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, and roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical reference for Redwood's Platform team covering systems & services inventory, operational how-tos, dashboards and alerting standards, production runbooks for core platform services, retrospective notes from major incidents in the last 12 months, and the 12-month roadmap and priorities. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform maintainers, service owners, and SRE partners.

Scope

- Systems included: API Gateway (redwood-api-gw), Router (request-router), Inference Router (inference-router), Batching Service (batch-coordinator), KV Cache (kv-cache), Telemetry pipeline (telemetry-ingest), Cluster Autoscaler (autoscaler), Tenant Control Plane (tenant-api).
- Excluded: experimental research infra, customer-managed private deployments (reference docs in eng-private-deployments).

Inventory: systems & owners

| Service | Purpose | Primary owner | Pager | SLOs |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| redwood-api-gw | Public REST/SDK ingress, rate-limiting | Platform API team | #platform-api-pager | 99.9% uptime; p95 latency < 120ms |
| request-router | Smart routing/fallbacks | Serving runtime team | #serving-runtime-pager | 99.95% uptime; p99 latency < 200ms |
| inference-router | Model variant routing | Serving runtime | #serving-runtime-pager | 99.9% uptime; error rate < 0.2% |
| batch-coordinator | Inference batching & queueing | Runtime scheduling | #runtime-batching | Queue latency p95 < 50ms; backlog < 5000 requests |
| kv-cache | Prefix/KV caching layer | Caching team | #cache-pager | Cache hit rate >= 70% for production workloads |
| telemetry-ingest | Logs & metrics pipeline | Observability team | #observability-pager | Ingest latency < 30s; retention 90d |
| autoscaler | GPU pool autoscaling | Infra-scaling team | #infra-ops | Scale-to-need within 120s for queued jobs |
| tenant-api | Customer control plane | Platform API team | #platform-api-pager | 99.95% uptime |

Standards: dashboards and alerts

Dashboard conventions
- Each service must expose a primary Service Overview dashboard with these panels: traffic (rps), error rate (5m/1h), latencies (p50/p95/p99), CPU/GPU utilization, queue/backlog counts, and recent deploys.
- Use common time ranges (1h/6h/24h/7d) and the standard color palette.
- Dashboards are owned in Grafana at grafana.redwood.internal (folder: /platform/<service>).

SLOs and Error Budget
- Default SLO template for critical platform services: Availability 99.95% (monthly), Latency p99 thresholds specified per-service.
- Error budget burn policy: any sustained burn > 10% in a 7-day window triggers an incident review and a temporary deployment freeze unless approved by Platform Eng manager.

Alerting standards
- Alert severities: P0 (SEV0) / P1 / P2. P0 alerts indicate customer impact or platform-wide outage, P1 indicates degraded service with partial impact.
- Alert format must include: summary, impacted services, required first action, runbook link, on-call roster.
- Example alerts per service:
  - redwood-api-gw: P0 if 50% of regional ingresses report 5xx rate > 2% for 2 minutes.
  - inference-router: P1 if p99 latency > 500ms for 5m AND error rate > 1%.
  - batch-coordinator: P1 if queue backlog > 5000 for 3m or average queue wait > 4s.
  - kv-cache: P2 if cache hit rate drops below 55% for 15m.

Alert thresholds (recommended starting values)
- P0: availability < 95% across all regions OR > 50% customer-facing 5xx.
- P1: service-specific threshold breach (latency/p99), or queue backlog threshold.
- P2: non-urgent degradations (metrics lag, minor error rate increases).

Playbook: common on-call runbook (first responder)

Steps for first responder (apply within 5 minutes of pageing):
1) Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty, update the alert with current status.
2) Check Service Overview dashboard and recent deploys.
3) Run health checks: 
   - curl -s -D- https://<service>-health/redwood | jq .status
   - kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=<service> -o wide
4) If traffic spike: confirm whether anomaly is customer-driven (spike in specific tenant) or global. Check request-router routing rules.
5) If increased errors after deploy: rollback the last deploy for the affected service and follow the rollback checklist.
6) If resource saturation (CPU/GPU): scale up nodes or enable burst capacity; notify infra-scaling team.
7) If unknown error pattern: collect traces and logs (see Collecting evidence below) and escalate to the service owner.
8) Open an incident in the incident tracker and assign an incident commander for SEV0/P0.

Runbooks: selected runbooks (shortened)

redwood-api-gw: High 5xx rate
- Symptoms: 5xx rate > 2% sustained for 2 minutes, p95 latency > 300ms.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Acknowledge alert.
  2) Verify recent deploys: grafana panel / CI tags. If deploy in last 30 minutes, rollback to previous stable tag (CI artifact ID).
  3) If no recent deploy, check rate-limiting config and upstream service health (tenant-api, request-router).
  4) If partial regional failure, failover traffic using traffic-router CLI: 
     redwoodctl traffic route set --service redwood-api-gw --region us-west-2 --action failover --target us-east-1
  5) If persistent, engage Platform API on-call and open SEV0.

batch-coordinator: Queue backlog growth
- Symptoms: backlog > 5000 or average wait > 4s.
- Steps:
  1) Increase batching concurrency: kubectl scale deployment batch-coordinator --replicas=$((current+2)) -n platform.
  2) Temporarily enable burst capacity policy (ops-policy: burst-enabled=true) for impacted tenant pools.
  3) If backlog persists, identify slow downstream model workers; re-route to fallback model variants.
  4) Notify customers if SLA will be impacted (use customer-comms template).

Rollback checklist (for deploy-related incidents)
1) Confirm failing metric corresponds to deployment timestamp.
2) Communicate intent to rollback in the incident thread and to PM/Support.
3) Use CI artifact tag to rollback: redwoodctl deploy rollback --service <svc> --tag <artifact> --reason "automated rollback due to metric degradation".
4) Monitor for 15 minutes; if stable, keep rollback and open a postmortem.

Collecting evidence (logs/traces/metrics)
- Logs: kubectl logs -l app=<service> -n platform --since=15m --tail=500 > /tmp/<service>-logs.txt\- For tenant-specific traces, query Tempo: trace_id query: service=<service> tenant=<tenant_id> timeframe=15m\- For request-level debugging, use request-id header x-request-id or traceparent from traces.

Retrospective notes (recent incidents and actions)

Incidents in the last 12 months (summary):
- 2025-05-18: region-wide routing regression (SEV0) \u2014 root cause: request-router config validation bug after canary; mitigating actions: immediate rollback, added config validation unit tests, introduced canary traffic cap (20%) and automated config linting.
- 2025-11-02: telemetry-ingest burst causing backpressure (P1) \u2014 root cause: spike in debug logs from a partner integration; mitigating actions: rate-limit ingest per-tenant, added late-binding buffering, increased ingest consumers.

Blameless follow-ups (action items)
1) Add config validation step to request-router CICD (owner: runtime scheduling; due: 2026-02-01).
2) Implement per-tenant ingest quotas in telemetry-ingest (owner: observability; due: 2026-03-15).
3) Improve deploy rollback automation to include automated canary score checks (owner: platform CI; due: 2026-04-01).

12-month roadmap & priorities (quarterly view)

Q1 2026:
- Deliver automated canary rollout with canary score gating for core platform services.
- Standardize dashboard templates and migrate all service dashboards to folder /platform/standardized.
- Pilot autoscaler burst capacity policies for Dedicated fleets.

Q2 2026:
- Roll out per-tenant telemetry quotas and alerting.
- Implement runbook-driven incident automation (auto-remediation for common failures).
- Improve batching heuristics for model families with high tail latencies.

Q3 2026:
- Expand platform observability to include model-level quality regressions and integrate with Redwood Optimize.
- Harden private-deployment runbooks for air-gapped upgrades.

Q4 2026:
- SLA productization: formalize enterprise SLA contracts for Dedicated customers and on-prem offers.
- Cost-optimization initiatives: quantization-aware routing and persistent prefix cache sizing.

Appendix A: CLI snippets and templates

- Collect logs (example):
  kubectl logs -l app=batch-coordinator -n platform --since=30m --tail=1000 > /tmp/batch-logs.txt

- Grafana dashboard export:
  grafana-cli dashboard export --folder "/platform/<service>" --dashboard-id <id> > /tmp/<service>-dashboard.json

- Customer communication template (short):
  Subject: Incident affecting <service> on <date>
  Body: Dear <customer>, we are investigating increased latency/errors for <service>. We expect remediation within X hours. We will provide updates every 30 minutes until resolved.

Appendix B: Change management & deploy freeze policy
- Any SEV0 or sustained error-budget burn > 10% for 7 days triggers a mandatory deploy freeze for non-critical changes.
- Exceptions require written approval from Platform Eng manager and SRE lead.

Document maintenance
- This page is reviewed quarterly by Platform Eng. Major updates must be recorded in the page change log and include reviewers.

For questions or contributions, open a PR on the platform wiki repo and assign reviewers Michael Chen and Ravi Kumar.
